observations.status: Source-backed reconciliation to existing 059 q2307/q2313 and earlier own Lens11 finding; no new unique finding.
source_trace: pr-working npz.rs:33–67: names/keys; contains, uncompressed_size, and array use exact-or-one-suffix matching; array decodes the found entry
95e npz.rs:17–29,45–86: get creates a private archive-bound NpzMember for the first match; its name, declared size, and decode all refer to that selected member; the query is kept for context
95e npz/name.rs:7–14,40–60: open query spelling; full match or one trailing .npy removal in archive order, not an exact-match-priority promise

observations.nonfinding: An earlier matching suffix entry can precede a later exact name; this is the documented first-match policy, not automatically a defect. Presence/get does not certify valid payload, decoded integrity, or allocation bounds. The current association avoids a second name lookup; this observation alone does not prove the historical second lookup produced mismatched metadata.

observations.status: Existing 059 q2316 CRC/declared-size/allocation policy question, not a new accepted unique finding.
source_trace: npz.rs:78–85: declared size exposed separately from decoding
zip/extent.rs:5–8,29–42: metadata admits u64 including zero and u64::MAX and converts to usize for native reservation
zip.rs:100–105,160–179: selected central declaration feeds Vec::with_capacity before Deflate read_to_end; output is owned and no limit appears in these displayed operations
mhr/correctives/archive.rs:10–15,38–78: file and owned byte inputs reach Npz; selected arrays are read for basis and sparse activation
observations.qualification: If a supported archive can present a sufficiently large declared decoded size to the selected Deflate path, the declaration reaches reservation before decoding and may cause allocation failure or capacity overflow; read_to_end has no explicit size bound in these lines. This is source reasoning only. rawzip admission for a particular archive, reachability through supported asset producers, Rust target/allocation behavior, trust boundary, and the intended resource or integrity policy are not independently established. No archive, fixture, parser, decompressor, product or simulation was run.
observations.related: q2316 already names declared size, CRC and allocation policy; q627 preserves caller/resource questions. Earlier 059 native source assessments retain their own scope; this reader has not inspected rawzip, flate2, integrity verification or actual data. The bounded current MHR source establishes a path, not permission to accept untrusted inputs or a vulnerability finding.
observations.future_direction: After an explicit asset trust/resource/integrity policy is chosen and native admission traced, establish bounded allocation/decoding and appropriate mismatch or integrity handling in the owning layer, without treating declaration as verified payload. Repair and acceptance checks are later work.

nonfindings: NpzArrayName and ArchiveMemberName represent query and actual filename roles; their open text namespace and optional suffix do not require a closed business enum.
NpzMember borrows the selected archive and retains the selected entry; decoded data may still fail later, so get/size are not a validation certificate.

MHR distinguishes activation and basis bytes and treats a missing basis as None; its sparse members are required. It adds contextual errors for selected arrays. This does not certify all shape, dtype, resource, native or GPU behavior.
Do not turn deliberately supported empty/case-sensitive/suffix/duplicate/member-order policies into a compatibility-fallback finding. Archived test source is read as text only.

Which rawzip and flate2 paths admit selected declarations and how should CRC, actual decoded length and resource limits be governed? Earlier 059 native-source evidence must be separately assessed with its original author and ranges.
What caller-level shape, numeric, joint and GPU contracts remain after NPZ parsing? Existing /root/mhr_character model findings and q172/q397–402 are related but not new NPZ identities.
Is any metadata-to-payload discrepancy or arbitrary memory pressure reachable from supported inputs in the intended environment? No product outcome or constructed archive is asserted.

thirteen_lenses.producer-propagation: MHR role-separated file/byte archives reach Npz get/array then NpyArray; wider shape/tensor consumers remain separately scoped.
thirteen_lenses.existing-type-owners: NpzArrayName, ArchiveMemberName and DeclaredUncompressedByteLength have distinct query, member and declared-metadata roles.
thirteen_lenses.admission-contracts: Archive presence and declared size do not imply payload validation or resource limits; NpyArray parsing is delegated and prior native scopes remain qualified.
thirteen_lenses.invariant-operations: Unverified u64 declaration converts to usize and drives Deflate reservation; resource policy and actual upstream admission remain open.
thirteen_lenses.aggregate-states: Private member handle retains archive and entry; metadata and decode use same selected entry rather than independently correlated public state.
thirteen_lenses.wrong-duplicate-owners: ZIP owns native storage/entry framing, NPZ owns array query, and MHR owns corrective array roles; representation similarity alone does not prove duplicate authority.
thirteen_lenses.redundant-authority: Directory size is explicit unverified metadata distinct from actual decoded payload; no automatic certificate or equality claim.
thirteen_lenses.behavior-preservation: First matching full-or-one-suffix query, query spelling, ordering, optional missing MHR basis and lazy decode are explicit; no compatibility shim inferred.
thirteen_lenses.enum-state-shape: MHR CorrectiveArray enum names fixed roles; missing basis is Option while decode errors are distinct, not a generic absence.
thirteen_lenses.derivability: Borrowed member with archive/entry identity has constructor invariants; NpzArrayName derives simple transparent traits without inventing membership.
thirteen_lenses.granularity: Declared bytes, parsed NPY shape, actual payload and MHR joint/feature indices are distinct quantities, not interchangeable merely as integers.
thirteen_lenses.raw-strings: Query text is an open native NumPy namespace, while MHR fixed keys are carried by CorrectiveArray; contextual diagnostic strings belong at presentation boundaries.
thirteen_lenses.raw-primitives: ZIP declaration is u64 with an explicit usize reservation conversion; actual NPY shapes and numeric values are separate contracts.
